items.title: Napoleonic What-if (Part 4)
items.summary: The final session of a Napoleonic game using General de Armee 2 follows a French Guard attack on a wooded flank and a costly cavalry fight in the centre. The report tracks how failing brigade rallies opened gaps and how casualties decided the result when time ran out.

items.title: Teeny Tiny Garigliano (an AAR)
items.summary: Le Coq Fou tries Battle Axe with a handful of bases on a new board. The small Garigliano scenario puts a Spanish crossing and an unprepared French force on the table, with a clear account of how the opening turns unfolded.

items.title: Hail Of Fire - a Normandy game
items.summary: Sgt Steiner tries adapting an Overlord scenario to Hail of Fire. The report explains where the rules’ hidden deployment and reserves work well, and where importing another ruleset’s force balance presents problems.

items.title: Peachtree Creek and Atlanta (ACW)
items.summary: A Bloody Big Battles scenario design account pairs Peachtree Creek and Atlanta, exploring what two related battles can offer a tabletop treatment of the 1864 campaign.

items.title: The next Portable Wargame Compendium: Yet another progress report
items.summary: Bob Cordery previews the next compendium, including a simple Peninsular War campaign, campaign games that fit in a tin, and a comparison of Portable and Coffeebreak Wargames. The post is a preview of the planned contents.

items.title: Thomas the Tank & Engine - Chinese Nationalists.
items.summary: A hobby bench post shows how a Soviet-pattern miniature train was adapted for Nationalist Chinese forces. It includes practical details about decals, the anti-aircraft crew, and fitting the rolling stock to existing 15mm track.

items.title: Anglo-Zulu forces on the tabletop and new backboard
items.summary: A foam-board backdrop painted with acrylics and chalk pastels gives the new collection a veldt horizon. The first outing adapts a One-Hour Wargames river-crossing scenario.

items.title: Remote wargame - Second Battle of Azukizaka, 1548
items.summary: A remote refight adapts Daniel Mersey’s Arrowstorm to Sengoku warfare. The house rules keep arquebusiers, ashigaru and samurai grouped, and the report shows how the shared command chart shapes play.

items.title: Friday Night at the Fights
items.summary: Jonathan Freitag ports the Commands & Colors: Ancients scenario for Orongis to Basic Impetvs. Keeping each army under one command makes this a focused comparison of how the same Punic Wars action plays under different rules.

items.title: AAR: More Russian Revolution
items.summary: A Setting the East Ablaze game puts a Bolshevik column in a Transcaspian valley. The designer reflects on how the route, variable movement, and a stalled vehicle skewed the scenario.

items.title: Scourge of Princes Renaissance Rules
items.summary: After two introductory games, the author assesses the rules and their supporting material, including how readily they accommodate different basing and figure scales. A companion to the army builder already in AI Discover.

items.title: Midgard Battle of Bosworth
items.source: Wargaming in 28 mm and Sometimes Smaller
items.summary: Six players refight Bosworth using Little Wars TV’s scenario and Midgard. The report covers assembling armies from several collections and making 3D-printed movement trays to bring the figures together.

items.title: Znaim 1809 - A Shadow of the Eagles game
items.summary: A club refight of the last major action of the 1809 campaign shows how a large battle was compressed for the tabletop and how simultaneous movement kept the game moving.

items.title: Ancient battle reports on small grids to playtest my own rules, part 2
items.summary: Shaun Travers tries the Allia River on grids as small as three by two, changing the forces and combat resolution after an early version proved flat. Useful for seeing what different grid sizes do to the same battle.

items.title: Aaaargh! — Agnadello 1509
items.summary: George Anderson revisits France versus Venice at Agnadello and notes where published scenario treatments disagree. It is a useful comparison for anyone building their own version of the battle.

items.title: Heinrichs in the hedgerows
items.summary: A company-sized Big Chain of Command game in Normandy uses the Le Bon Repos scenario. It shows how a two-phase action handles objectives, tactical withdrawal, and redeployment between phases.

items.title: Ten Knights for Greathelm Medieval Skirmish Game
items.summary: A medieval skirmish project paints ten Footsore and Gripping Beast foot knights in contrasting liveries for Greathelm, including shield motifs, metallic highlights and practical batch-painting lessons.

items.title: Painting Challenge: Late November Update
items.summary: A varied historical miniature painting roundup includes 20mm Shermans prepared for Burma, British airborne figures, medieval mounted serjeants and small village terrain, with practical notes on figure storage.

items.title: Destroyed Forest Terrain for Toys for Tots
items.summary: A quick terrain-painting project transforms 3D-printed ruined woodland using wet-blended muddy earth and UV-resin water effects. The techniques offer ideas for building atmospheric scatter terrain.

items.title: Ticinus River 218 BC - Command and Colors Ancients Game
items.summary: A solo refight puts Hannibal’s cavalry against Republican Rome. The unequal command hands and leaders give a concrete starting point for designing an early Second Punic War scenario.

items.title: Breeds Hill 1775 - Rebels & Patriots
items.summary: A small-scale Breed’s Hill refight uses Rebels & Patriots with longer artillery ranges and activation chits for three commands per side. Stalled flank activations change the pace of the assault.

items.title: Germantown, 4 October 1777 — Eastern flank
items.summary: The third game in a four-part Germantown campaign shifts attention to the eastern flank. The Black Powder report lists the forces and shows how an earlier game shaped the next scenario.

items.title: HMGS Fall In 2026: Convention Recap, Battle Reports & Photos
items.summary: A convention host recaps the five games he ran and one he played, spanning Second World War gaming and a retro sci-fi adaptation of Combat Patrol.

items.title: Battle of New Market 1864 - Valor and Fortitude Game
items.summary: A Canberra club uses Valor and Fortitude to refight New Market. The report follows five players across two sides and shows the miniature terrain around the town.

items.title: V&F - Roughly Rolica
items.summary: A compact 6mm Valour and Fortitude scenario supplies an order of battle and a clear dilemma. The French rearguard must delay a stronger force before a flanking column gets behind it.

items.title: The Battle of Lützen, 2nd May 1813
items.summary: A substantial scenario for Napoleon’s Battles, with a historical briefing, forces, and scenario rules adapted to the fourth edition.

items.title: Year of the Four Emperors - Roman Civil War Strength and Honour Game
items.summary: An older 2mm Strength and Honour refight pits two Roman armies of equal points but different troop quality against each other. It also shows how little storage space the army takes up.

items.title: King, Republic & Empire
items.summary: Seven players gather for a fast-moving 15mm DBA evening spanning Wars of the Roses armies, Republican Romans against Epirotes, and Seleucids against Rome. Rotating matchups provide several distinct tactical puzzles in one session.

items.title: Rematch With Vol at Salem Church
items.summary: A second Salem Church game reverses the first narrow Confederate victory. Federal assaults briefly seize the church, counterattacks break two Union brigades, and a final coordinated push wrecks Semmes' brigade—a revealing test of ACW scenario balance.

items.title: Restless Natives: One of my earlier attempts to write a set of Colonial wargame rules
items.summary: Bob Cordery revisits a colonial ruleset designed for a sub-two-hour game on a 4-by-3-foot table. Playing cards govern activation, while event cards add bursts of movement, firepower and rallies; a smaller-table revision is under consideration.

items.title: October 2026 Report
items.summary: An unusually varied club diary covers Modern Spearhead, a Carlist Wars crossroads battle, linked Viking raids, samurai and Elchingen. Especially useful is the example of branching skirmish scenarios where the first raid's outcome determines the follow-up.

items.title: The Battle of Wittenberg, 2nd October 1760 (The Game)
items.summary: The follow-up to the published Wittenberg scenario puts Prussian redoubts under pressure from the larger Reichsarmee. The 15mm Tricorn refight shows how artillery, delayed orders and shifting flank threats can make an unequal battle interesting.

items.title: Impudent Mortal Brick Walls for Toys for Tots
items.summary: A quick terrain-painting sequence turns brick wall sections into weathered cover: red primer, mottled brown sprays, a black-and-white oil wash, flock and aged posters. The methods transfer readily to ruined historical town walls.

items.title: Italy 1943 - I Haven't The Foggia'st - Monty's Casino Campaign Turn 1
items.summary: A British advance off the Foggia plain opens a 1943 mini-campaign. One reconnaissance unit works around the flank while the main force attacks a rocky outcrop, giving the game two linked problems on the same table.

items.title: Du mont Suribachi aux côteaux de la Marne: Iwo Jima 3D
items.summary: This French-language photo report shows a three-dimensional Memoir ’44 table with a fortified Mount Suribachi, hidden Japanese positions, and a buried tank. The narrow finish makes the airfield’s value as a victory objective easy to see.

items.title: Battle of Lal 2444BC
items.summary: A Mesopotamian tabletop pursuit comes down to two canal crossings and a hill the army of Ur must hold on turn 13. The report shows how terrain gives chariots, spearmen, and light bowmen distinct jobs.

items.title: Siege of Tobruk
items.source: 20mm Crimean War Wargaming and Other Stuff
items.summary: An enlarged Command and Colors map becomes an 8-by-4-foot Tobruk table with 3-inch hexes. The setup shows how the ditch, minefields, strongpoints, and armoured reserve fit together before the first turn.

items.title: Scourge of Princes: Army Builder
items.summary: Vexillia built basic and advanced army-list spreadsheets for Scourge of Princes. The sheets check artillery and formation limits as you build a force, making it easier to compare two plausible Italian Wars armies before setting up a game.

items.title: The Battle of Monocacy After Action Report – Unioncon 2026!
items.summary: For a Monocacy convention game, the host shapes hills with foam under a mat and lays the rivers and roads on top. The Union gets freedom to redeploy, and the players’ decision to defend forward turns the two bridges into the focus of the game.

imageRights.alt: Miniature armies on the Monocacy convention table.

items.title: The Battle of Wittenberg, 2nd October 1760 (The Scenario)
items.summary: A Seven Years War scenario for Tricorn gives the outnumbered Prussians a defensible position and the Reichsarmee the challenge of bringing its strength to bear. The map, deployments, and historical background show how to turn a lopsided battle into a playable one.
